brief.question: Rebuild AutoHotkeyUX (the AutoHotkey Dash and its tool windows) in Rust with the same look, running on Arch Linux + KDE Plasma.
brief.purpose: Port for personal use on Linux
brief.done_when: A Rust/egui app in app/ builds, shows the Dash, New Script, Launch Config, Editor selection and Window Spy windows matching the originals, with Linux equivalents of Windows-only actions.

findings.statement: AutoHotkeyUX.exe is the stock AutoHotkey v2.0.19 64-bit interpreter (version resource; same hash as v2\AutoHotkey64.exe in installed-files.csv); the visible app (Dash, New Script, Launch Config, Editor, Window Spy) is defined by the .ahk scripts in the UX folder.

handoff: Rust/egui rebuild in app/ (Dash, New Script, Launch Config, Editor select, Window Spy, launcher --run, version picker). Builds on Windows; `cargo check --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` passes. rebuild_check round 0 passed (build + screenshot). Original windows pictured in app/shots/original-*.png; ours via `--screenshot f --window dash|new|launch|editor|spy`. Open: Window Spy and file associations untested on real KDE; syntax detection simplified. Next ideas: test on Arch, KDE service menu "New AutoHotkey script", tray icon.
